metadata.title: Billionaire Republican megadonor Ron Lauder reportedly stopped donating to the GOP

sources.news_title: A Billionaire GOP Megadonor Has Abruptly Stopped Donating
sources.text:
Ronald Lauder, the New York cosmetics heir long known as a political ATM for state Republicans, has apparently snapped his wallet shut. The 82-year-old billionaire—who poured nearly $13 million into 2022 races and causes that aided a GOP House flip and gave $1 million to an anti-Zohran Mamdani super PAC—has not given a cent to New York Republicans this year, records show. His once-active super PAC is dormant, and his longtime team of political operatives has been dismissed, reports Nicholas Fandos for the New York Times.
                                    
                                    
                                
                                
                             
                            
                            
                            
                            
                            
                                
                                
                                    
                                        Fandos digs into what may be driving the about-face. Associates say family pressure and a desire to streamline his commitments for the "last years" of his life are driving the pullback; a source says he and his adult daughters have agreed to "prioritize art and philanthropic projects that could secure his legacy," writes Fandos. Others note the Estée Lauder stock that underpins much of his wealth has plunged from its 2021 peak. As for whether another New York donor can fill the gap, the chairman of the New York Conservative Party puts it plainly: "The simple answer is no." Read the full piece here.

sources.news_title: One Of The GOP’s Biggest New York Donors Is Sitting Out
sources.text:
New York Republicans could be entering the 2026 midterms without their biggest financial backer after billionaire Ronald Lauder reportedly stopped donating to GOP candidates in the state.
Lauder, 82, an heir to the Estée Lauder fortune, has been one of New York Republicans’ most prolific donors. He has contributed more than $40 million to state and federal races over the past several decades and maintained a close relationship with President Donald Trump dating back to their time together at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton Business School.
According to The New York Times, Lauder has not made a single political donation to New York Republicans this year. His most recent political contributions included a $5 million donation to pro-Trump super PAC MAGA Inc. and support for another super PAC that opposed Zohran Mamdani’s campaign for New York City mayor
Lauder has also been credited with helping persuade Trump to pursue the idea of purchasing Greenland.
Gerard Kassar, chairman of the Conservative Party of New York State, told the Times that Lauder’s family encouraged him to step back from politics as he has gotten older.
Kassar said that Lauder “got to a certain age that his family and him all decided he wasn’t going to be as active the way he has been.”
Kassar added that no one can replace Lauder as a financial backer for Republicans in New York, describing the philanthropist as a one-stop shop for GOP fundraising in the state.
The Times cited three associates of Lauder who echoed Kassar’s account, saying Lauder’s children had urged him to reduce his spending on politics, philanthropy, and art collecting.
Lauder’s retreat comes despite his son-in-law, Kevin Warsh, taking one of Washington’s most consequential jobs. Warsh, who married Lauder’s daughter Jane in 2002, became chairman of the Federal Reserve after being nominated by President Trump earlier this year.
Kassar said he was unaware whether Lauder’s personal finances played any role in his decision to reduce his political giving.
Lauder has also downsized his personal political operation, recently eliminating staff from his personal office. Securities filings from The Estée Lauder Companiesshow that Lauder reimbursed the company nearly $22 million in 2025 for expenses associated with that office, suggesting it had become a sizable operation.
Separately, Lauder made headlines in 2023 when he suspended donations to his alma mater, the University of Pennsylvania, over its handling of antisemitism on campus following pro-Palestinian demonstrations.
“I’ve spent the last 40 years of my life fighting antisemitism all over the world,” Lauder said. “I never in my wildest imagination thought I would have to fight it at my own university, my alma mater, my family’s alma mater.”
He added that he and other donors ‘can no longer be silent,’ and that newspapers, universities, and cable channels had to understand ‘there are consequences for their actions. The University has hosted numerous pro-Palestinian demonstrations and protests on its campus since the October 7 attacks.

sources.news_title: Trump Pal Ronald Lauder Is Cutting Off the GOP
sources.text:
Billionaire Ronald Lauder has spent decades writing checks to Republicans, giving some $40 million to the party in the last ten years alone, including $5 million to MAGA, Inc., last year. But unfortunately for Republicans, it appears that the cosmetics heir and Donald Trump’s friend of 50 years is done bankrolling the party — though not for the reason you might expect!
Lauder, who is worth an estimated $4.9 billion thanks to the makeup company his mother founded, has reportedly not made a single donation to the GOP this year, according to the New York Times. The outlet reports that he has also “quietly dismissed a stable of well-paid advisers, ad makers and other consultants who regularly reported to his personal office in the Estée Lauder headquarters overlooking Central Park in Manhattan,” some of whom had worked for him for more than 30 years. Why the sudden shift? Has Lauder had a change of heart about the party of Trump in general or perhaps Donald Trump specifically, both of which have given people a clown car’s worth of reasons not to support them, from reports of widespread corruption to human-rights abuses to dousing D.C. in gold? Just to be clear, the answer is no; Lauder is seemingly fine with all that.
Instead, his abrupt turn in financial support appears to be a result of his adult daughters — one of whom is married to Trump’s new Fed chair, Kevin Warsh — sitting their dad down and having an uncomfortable talk about money, or at least as uncomfortable as a talk about money can be when everyone in the room is a billionaire.
Per the Times:
Three associates said that Mr. Lauder recently confided in them, saying that his adult children have stepped in to try to reduce his lavish spending on politics, art and philanthropy and suggesting reluctantly that he could not spend what he once did. The associates pointed to public securities filings showing that his stake in the family business, Estée Lauder, has lost at least $1.2 billion in value as the stock plummeted 77 percent from its 2021 high.
An individual close to the family — who “did not dispute that Mr. Lauder’s political spending was being curtailed” — insisted to the Times that the shift was not about conserving money but had more to do with the billionaire “and his adult children [agreeing] that he would simplify the reach of his activities — involving extensive travel, large paid staff and public speeches — as he prepared for the last years of his life in order to prioritize art and philanthropic projects that could secure his legacy.” Yet he’s also been in selling mode, shedding a Manhattan home for $20 million and 30 acres of land in East Hampton for $56 million and putting a fleet of WWII fighter planes on the market. He also merged his showcase for German and Austrian art, Neue Galerie, with the Metropolitan Museum of Art, a move expected to save him millions annually in operating expenses.
Lauder — who, it should be forever noted, gave Trump the idea to buy Greenland — did not respond to a list of questions from the Times. In a statement, he declared he’d used his monetary giving to “strengthen” New York City, adding, “I intend to continue dedicating my time, resources and energy to advancing those democratic principles and to ensuring that New York remains a place where people, families, businesses and communities can thrive.” (Last year, he gave $1 million to a super-PAC trying to defeat Zohran Mamdani’s bid for office.)
While Lauder’s lack of giving is expected to have a meaningful effect on Republicans in New York, they’ll clearly be fine outside the five boroughs as other MAGA-supporting billionaires plow money into the midterm elections. Elon Musk has reportedly committed to spending upwards of $100 to $120 million in support of Republican candidates running this November, and other major donors have spent more than $880 million in the hopes of stopping Democrats from retaking Congress.
For his part, it’s of course possible that Lauder could choose to resume donations in the future, particularly if he feels pressure from Trump, who would undoubtedly have no qualms about trashing the guy on Truth Social until he opens up his checkbook again.

sources.news_title: Billionaire GOP megadonor abruptly pulls the plug on Republicans ahead of midterms
sources.text:
One of the Republican Party’s biggest financial backers is suddenly keeping his wallet closed, and the timing couldn’t be more awkward for the GOP.
Ronald Lauder, the billionaire heir to the Estée Lauder fortune and one of the Republican Party’s most reliable megadonors, has abruptly stopped making political donations ahead of this year’s critical midterm elections, according to The New York Times.
The 82-year-old billionaire, whose fortune is estimated at nearly $5 billion, has not contributed to Republican causes in his home state of New York this year after spending decades writing massive checks to conservative candidates and organizations.
The news comes as Republicans brace for a difficult November, with Democrats hoping to regain control of Congress and deal a major political blow to Donald Trump.
A Democratic takeover of the House could also open the door to new investigations—and potentially even another impeachment effort against the president.
But despite the unfortunate timing for Republicans, people close to Lauder say politics isn’t the reason he stopped writing checks.
Instead, sources told The New York Times that Lauder’s adult children persuaded him to slow down as he enters his 80s, encouraging him to scale back his political activity, reduce his staff, and spend more time focusing on philanthropy and his world-renowned art collection.
Lauder also stepped down from Estée Lauder’s board of directors in early 2025 as part of that broader shift away from public life.
“Can anyone replace him in New York financially?” New York Conservative Party Chairman Gerard Kassar told the newspaper. “The simple answer is no.”
That’s a sobering reality for Republicans.
Over the years, Lauder has poured more than $40 million into state and federal political campaigns, including a $5 million donation to Trump’s MAGA Inc. super PAC in 2025 and another $1 million to a super PAC opposing Democratic socialist Zohran Mamdani’s mayoral campaign.
His relationship with Trump stretches back decades. Lauder has even been credited with encouraging Trump’s long-running interest in purchasing Greenland.
Still, Lauder insists he’s not abandoning the causes he believes in.
In a statement to The New York Times, he said his political giving has always been aimed at strengthening New York and promoting democratic principles, adding that he plans to continue devoting his “time, resources and energy” to those goals, even if he’s no longer opening his checkbook to Republican candidates.

sources.news_title: GOP-Backer Ronald Lauder Stops Political Donating
Billionaire Republican Megadonor Pulls the Plug on Trump’s Party
sources.text:
Ronald Lauder, the billionaire and major GOP donor, has abruptly stopped handing out political donations ahead of the crucial midterm elections for Donald Trump.
The wealthy heir to the Estée Lauder cosmetics fortune has tightened his purse strings and has not donated to any Republican causes in his home state of New York this year, The New York Times reported.
Lauder, who has an estimated net worth of around $4.9 billion, has closed his checkbook just as the GOP is expected to suffer heavy defeats in November’s nationwide elections. The ramifications of an electoral wipeout for the Republican Party would be significant for Trump if a Democratic-controlled Congress were to pursue impeachment proceedings against the president.
However, the 82-year-old’s change in spending habits does not appear to be linked to dissatisfaction with Trump or the GOP as a whole.
Instead, sources told the Times that Lauder’s adult children had convinced him to curtail his lavish spending and public activities as he enters his later years. That includes cutting back on political donations, downsizing staff, and giving fewer public speeches.
In January 2025, Lauder—whose daughter Jane is married to Federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh—announced he would be retiring from the Estée Lauder Board of Directors.
Lauder is also hoping to prioritize art and philanthropic projects, which he believes will form a greater part of his legacy.
Gerard Kassar, chairman of the New York Conservative Party, said a close associate told him that Lauder had “got to a certain age that his family and him all decided he wasn’t going to be as active the way he has been.”
“Can anyone replace him in New York financially?” Kassar told the Times. “The simple answer is no.”
Lauder remained politically active last year, including donating $5 million to MAGA Inc., a super PAC backing Trump, in March 2025. He previously handed $200,000 to Trump’s 2024 presidential campaign.
He also donated another $1 million to a super PAC opposing Democratic socialist Zohran Mamdani’s mayoral campaign.
Lauder’s ties to Trump date back decades, and he is credited with putting the idea in the president’s head to try to purchase Greenland back in 2018. Estée Lauder’s headquarters is just two blocks away from Trump Tower on New York’s 5th Avenue.
Overall, Lauder is estimated to have donated more than $40 million to state and federal campaigns. However, that pales in comparison to what he has spent on artwork. In 2006, the billionaire paid $135 million for Gustav Klimt’s Portrait of Adele Bloch-Bauer I, the highest price ever paid for a painting at the time.
In a statement to the Times, Lauder said he has used his political donations to “strengthen” New York City.
He added: “I intend to continue dedicating my time, resources and energy to advancing those democratic principles and to ensuring that New York remains a place where people, families, businesses and communities can thrive.”
The Daily Beast has contacted Ronald Lauder’s office for comment.

“For decades, Ronald S. Lauder, the billionaire cosmetics heir and philanthropist, has been something like a one-man bank for Republicans in New York,” the New York Times reports.
“He personally funded a campaign to impose term limits in New York City, helped pay for a lawsuit to overturn the state’s gerrymandered congressional map and, just four years ago, plowed close to $13 million into races that helped Republicans flip the House.”
“Now, in the middle of another crucial midterm election year, Mr. Lauder, 82, appears to have abruptly closed his political checkbook, and the ramifications for the conservative movement he has nurtured in his home state could be significant.”
